62.steps:
1). Login to the FW as admin from the default LAN interface;
2). Navigate to Network>Interfaces page, configure an interface X2 to DMZ zone, choose the IP assignment as Static Mode, and input valid IP, make sure the operation is successful;
3). Go to the Network>Zone, make sure the X2 is listed in the "Interface" column of DMZ zone;
4). Go to the Network>Address Object, make sure the zones of "X2 IP" and "X2 Subnet" are DMZ;
5). Go to the Network>Routing, make sure the interface X2 of the Route Advisement table is marked as DMZ zone;
6). Go to the Firewall>Access Rules, in the DMZ to WAN matrix, modify the default rule to have "Everyone" as Allowed Users;
7). From the PC2, ping a PC one WAN side, notice no reply received;
8). Go to Log>View, check there is an "ICMP is dropped according rules" log, with "DMZ >WAN" in the Rules column.
9). Repeat the steps on another unassigned interface;

63.steps:
1). Login to the FW;
2). Configure the WAN interface to setup connection with lab network;
3). Open the configure dialog of the DMZ interface and choose the "Transparent Mode", create an address range which is inside the WAN subnet but don't include the WAN interface IP, and choose it as transparent range, click OK, make sure the change is applied;
4). At this time, make PC1 can not access the DMZ interface anymore;
5). Change the IP address of the PC1 to be inside the transparent range, make sure the FW can be accessed from PC1 again;
6). In the Interfaces Table, make sure the IP Assignment of the DMZ interface is Transparent Mode instead of Static;
7). Assign another interface to DMZ zone, and repeat the steps.
